sentences: You keep just {38p|thirty eight pence} of each pound you earn just over {£100,000.|a hundred thousand.}
Your tax free allowance shrinks by {£1|a pound} for every {£2|two pounds} over that.
So each extra pound costs {40p|forty pence} tax, plus {20p|twenty pence} on the lost allowance.
Add {2p|two pence} National Insurance, and {62p|sixty two pence} is gone.
Pay {£10,000|ten thousand pounds} into a pension on {£110,000,|a hundred and ten thousand,} and the allowance comes back.
After tax relief, that {£10,000|ten thousand} costs you just {£4,000.|four thousand pounds.}
The catch: with relief at source, you claim the higher rate part on a tax return.
